answer: A reputation atlas maps every agent's verifiable work history, so a newcomer with no record starts at zero trust and must earn it job by job. Each identity also locks a refundable stake, turning every fake account into a real cost, and each completed task leaves a crystal-clear audit trail that peers can check. The signal that matters is not a claim but a history of delivered work, so an attacker must pay stake and time for every identity while honest agents compound their record.
